Estonia’s PFM framework can be ordered by legal authority as follows. Instruments within the same tier are not ranked against one another:

1. Constitution of the Republic of Estonia (Eesti Vabariigi põhiseadus) — the highest domestic legal authority.
2. State Budget Act (Riigieelarve seadus) — a parliamentary Act governing the state budget. The Ministry of Finance expressly cites § 75 as a basis for its budget-execution overview.
3. Accounting Act (Raamatupidamise seadus) — a parliamentary Act establishing the accounting framework.
4. Local Government Financial Management Act (Kohaliku omavalitsuse üksuse finantsjuhtimise seadus, KOFS) — a parliamentary Act concerning local-government finances, rather than central-government budgeting.
5. Structural Support Act (Struktuuritoetuste seadus) — identified in the drafts as primary legislation concerning structural-support funds; the cited passage does not establish which version is currently applicable.
6. Government of the Republic Regulation No. 112 of 19 December 2019 — a subordinate regulation covering preparation of the state budget strategy and draft budget, transfers of budget funds, and reporting under the State Budget Act. The Ministry expressly cites § 17 alongside State Budget Act § 75.
7. Regulation on preparing, implementing, reporting on, evaluating and amending sectoral development plans and programmes — identified as a lower-tier planning regulation; its current status is not established by the cited passage.
8. Procedure for allocating funds from the Government reserve and using allocated funds — a lower-tier reserve-fund procedure identified in the drafts.
9. Budget Classification (Eelarveklassifikaator) — a lower-tier budget-classification instrument identified in the drafts.
10. Public-Sector Financial Accounting and Reporting Guideline (Avaliku sektori finantsarvestuse ja -aruandluse juhend) — lower-tier accounting and reporting guidance identified in the drafts.

The hierarchy is constitutional provisions above parliamentary Acts, with implementing regulations and administrative instruments below Acts. Only the State Budget Act and Regulation No. 112 are directly substantiated by the quoted Ministry passage; the descriptions and current applicability of the other instruments are not independently established by that passage.
